page: Microsoft Azure M8-4ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MS server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration allocates 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. A key characteristic of this server is its massive memory capacity of 219.0 GB, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 54.69 GB per core. It also includes 262 GB of local SSD storage and is premium storage capable, though it does not bundle any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals significant performance tradeoffs. Despite the large memory footprint, the server exhibits limited processing power and memory throughput. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1035.08 falls in the bottom 10%, while the multi-core score of 2724.76 is in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block transfers registering at 17.71 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 17.19 GB/sec. Similarly, Geekbench and Passmark CPU scores place the instance in the lower performance tiers. These metrics indicate that while the server can hold vast datasets in memory, it is not designed for high-throughput computational tasks or rapid data processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the M8-4ms offers a highly specialized resource density, trading raw CPU performance and memory speed for sheer memory capacity. This makes it a cost-effective choice for workloads that are strictly memory-bound rather than compute-bound. Appropriate workloads include large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise legacy applications with high RAM requirements, caching layers, and database operations that fit entirely within the 219.0 GB memory space but require minimal CPU cycles.
description: Microsoft Azure M8-4ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for memory-intensive workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor running at 2.7 GHz, it provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores on the x86_64 architecture. The server is characterized by an exceptionally high memory capacity of 219.0 GB, paired with 262 GB of local SSD storage. However, benchmark results indicate significant performance tradeoffs, with CPU and memory bandwidth metrics consistently scoring in the lower percentiles, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 1970.0 and a large-block memory read bandwidth of 17.71 GB/sec. Consequently, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive RAM density rather than raw computational speed. It is best suited for large in-memory databases, caching layers, and memory-bound enterprise applications with low CPU demands.
